prompt: Some people think traditional games are better than modern games in helping children develop their abilities. To what extent do you agree?
essay:
Some people argue that traditional games are more effective than modern games in developing children's abilities. I partly agree with this view because traditional games are particularly useful for physical and social development, although modern games can also improve problem-solving and strategic thinking.

On the one hand, traditional games can be highly effective in developing children's physical and social abilities. Many traditional activities require children to move, cooperate with others and follow shared rules. For example, outdoor team games encourage children to run, communicate and work together to achieve a common goal. By taking part in these activities, children can improve their physical fitness while also learning cooperation and patience. Such games can also prevent children from spending excessive amounts of time sitting indoors. Therefore, traditional games remain valuable for children's overall development.

On the other hand, modern games can also help children develop abilities that are useful in contemporary life. Many computer and strategy games require players to solve problems, make decisions and plan several steps ahead. For instance, a strategy-based game may require a child to manage limited resources and choose the most effective way to achieve a goal. These activities can strengthen logical thinking and decision-making skills. However, excessive gaming may reduce physical activity if children spend too much time indoors. Thus, modern games should complement rather than completely replace traditional physical activities.

In conclusion, I partly agree that traditional games are better because they promote physical activity and social interaction. Nevertheless, modern games can also develop problem-solving and strategic thinking, so children can benefit from a balanced combination of both types.
